title: Pressure-induced s,p-d electron redistribution accompanies structural transformation in amorphous Zr-Cu alloy under compression
authors: P. Dziegielewski, J. Antonowicz, K. Georgarakis, O. Lord, M. Amboage, D. Daisenberger, L. Clough, T. Irifune, T. Shinmei
abstract: Extreme compression can reorganize atomic valence states, in some regimes driving charge from spatially extended orbitals into more compact ones. We investigate this effect in amorphous Zr67Cu33 metallic glass by combining high-pressure X-ray absorption fine structure measurements up to 69 GPa with molecular dynamics simulations and density functional theory calculations. The Zr K-edge XANES spectra show a pronounced increase in the pre-edge intensity and a change in its pressure dependence, whereas the Cu response is markedly weaker. Molecular-dynamics simulations reproduce the measured EXAFS spectra and provide reliable input for the electronic-structure calculations. The calculated Mulliken populations reveal pressure-induced depletion of Zr s and p-states, accompanied by an increase of the d-state population, while the density of states indicates enhanced p-d hybridization under compression. These results provide experimental and computational evidence for pressure-induced s,p-d electronic redistribution in zirconium and link this effect to the previously reported anomalous structural evolution of the compressed amorphous alloy.
summary: This paper experimentally and computationally investigates how compressing an amorphous $	ext{Zr-Cu}$ metallic glass alters its electronic structure. By analyzing XANES spectra and performing DFT calculations, the authors demonstrate a systematic redistribution of valence electrons from s and p orbitals into the d-band under high pressure. This links the observed electronic changes to the material's structural evolution.
main_problem: The study investigates how extreme compression induces electronic structure changes, specifically electron redistribution, in amorphous metallic alloys.
main_result: The research provides evidence for pressure-induced s,p-d electronic redistribution in zirconium, characterized by depletion of s and p-states and an increase in d-state population.
method: The work combines high-pressure X-ray Absorption Near-Edge Structure (XANES) measurements with Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations and Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is the amorphous $	ext{Zr}_{67}	ext{Cu}_{33}$ metallic glass, studied under compression up to 69 GPa. The theoretical framework involves analyzing orbital hybridization and charge transfer mechanisms.
key_observables: XANES pre-edge intensity, Mulliken populations ($	ext{s, p, d}$ orbital populations), Density of States (DOS), and Pair Distribution Functions ($	ext{PDFs}$).
important_parameters: Pressure range up to 69 GPa; specific breakpoints identified for electronic changes (e.g., 32 GPa for $	ext{Zr}$ s-electron depletion).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on interpreting spectral shape changes (pre-edge intensity) as evidence of hybridization, and uses the Mulliken scheme for charge analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate XANES spectra showing pre-edge evolution, comparisons between experimental and simulated EXAFS spectra, and plots detailing charge transfer ($\Delta q$) and orbital-resolved populations across pressure.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of presenting experimental XANES data, validating local structure using MD/EXAFS, and finally interpreting the electronic changes using DFT calculations to quantify s,p-d electron redistribution.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter, the study of electronic structure evolution under extreme conditions and the use of advanced computational techniques (DFT/MD) to model complex, disordered materials is relevant to understanding highly correlated or disordered quantum systems.
